contributions.anchor: Form A's own printed 'Total Contributions: (to line 1. of report): 4,067.20' on p3, equal to the cover's LINE 1 cells (Totals for This Report 4,067.20 = Cumulative 4,067.20)
contributions.detail: 5 Form A rows (1,000.00 + 250.00 + 250.00 + 200.00 + 2,367.20) sum to 4,067.20 exactly = the schedule's printed total = the cover's line-1 This-Report and Cumulative cells, which are equal because the Last Report column is the filer's own '-' nil mark throughout (this is the filer's first report of the cycle). THE LINE-1/LINE-2 BASIS RULE: this is the 4-line form, so Form A itemizes only line 1 (donors above $50) and the residual against the published stated_total_contributions would be line 2 - but here line 2 (the <=$50 aggregate) is also printed '-', a NIL MARK, so there is no residual at all and no unitemized remainder to explain. Per the zero-glyph ruling the '-' cells stay BLANK, never 0. No in-kind rows are labelled, so both in-kind conventions give the same figure.

itemized.escalation_note: Seven crops. THREE were exploratory and are the reason this filing took longer than its 16 rows suggest: both schedules are rotated sheets on which the ROWS RUN RIGHT-TO-LEFT in the rendered page (row 1 is at the RIGHT edge, next to the header strip), which no other filing in this chunk does, and my first two probes at the left-hand bands came back blank because I had assumed the usual left-to-right order. A full-width strip crop of the amount column (pct:0,80,100,20@p2) settled the orientation by showing all eleven amounts descending right-to-left. FOUR were A3 proofs, two per schedule page: p2 row 1 rendered '$500.00' and row 11 rendered '$150'; p3 row 1 rendered '$1,000.00' and row 5 rendered '$2,367.20'. No legibility escalation was needed - both sides closed exactly on the first full-page read.
